data.name: Nirvana: The First Travel
data.detailed_description:
Nirvana was a company specialized in gravity research. At first, all they had was a spinning room, and the desire to, one day, be able to manipulate space-time, and therefore, gravity itself. Then came the day: they finally made it! All the equations were right, and that led the Nirvana Facility to prosperous times... for around two hours. Gravity could do so much more than deform space time, so much more... and they found it in a "not so good" way. They ended up colliding their dimension with someone else's, opening a very unexpected gateway. What, or who, did they find in the other side?

The puzzles on this game usually present you with a situation, with no obvious way out. You must use all the resources at you disposal to proceed, and keep moving foward. You play as Tom Walker, a security guard that wakes up in an empty room inside the Nirvana Facility soon after an emergency evacuation. Right at the beginning, you meet the familiar voice of Doctor Lestrade, the man to instruct you through the various puzzles the facility presents. The puzzles involve interesting gravity shifts, and a gun that can move heavy objects, create anti-gravitational spheres and teleport Walker around.

reviews.review:
[h1]Overall Score: 5/10[/h1]

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
[list]
    [*][b]Interesting game mechanics.[/b] The gun mechanics have been thought out well, and are quite different from other games. The rotating rooms and redirectors are an interesting challenge in themselves.
    [*][b]Nice graphics.[/b] 
    [*][b]Fun puzzles.[/b] 
    [*][b]Cheap.[/b] €3.49 at the time this was written. Even if you don't really like the game it's not a huge loss.
[/list]

[h1]Cons:[/h1]
[list]
    [*][b]Very short.[/b] 2 hours at most.
    [*][b]Controls feel slow.[/b] The gun doesn't follow your movements like in most games, but instead lags behind you a bit, making it feel disjointed. The jumping is also a bit dodgy. Half of the time I died was because I just walked into one of the pits without jumping.
    [*][b]Poor voice acting.[/b] I'm pretty sure this was just voiced by the developer, and the lackluster delivery makes the story seem bland and uninteresting.
    [*][b]Broken interactions/textures.[/b] While using the red sphere I managed to accidentally teleport myself out of the map and started falling into oblivion. Towards the end there is a blatantly missing floor that makes you wonder if you're going the wrong way.
    [*][b]No controller support.[/b] It really feels like the kind of game that would benefit from a controller.
[/list]
